verses.text: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily on people:

God gives a person riches, wealth, and honor, so that they have everything their heart wants. But God does not give them the power to enjoy it, and a stranger enjoys it instead. This is meaningless, and it is a terrible sickness.
A man may have a hundred children and live many years. But if his heart is not filled with good things, and he does not even get a proper burial, I say a baby born dead is better off than he is.
For the baby comes for nothing and leaves in darkness, and its name is covered in darkness.
It has never seen the sun or known anything. Yet it has more rest than that man.
Even if he lives a thousand years twice over but does not enjoy good things, do not all go to the same place?
All the hard work people do is for their mouths, and yet their hunger is never satisfied.
For what advantage does a wise person have over a fool? What does a poor person gain by knowing how to live before others?
It is better to enjoy what your eyes can see than to keep wanting more. This too is meaningless, like chasing the wind.
Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what people are. No one can argue with someone who is stronger than they are.
The more words there are, the more meaningless they become. How does that help anyone?
For who knows what is good for people in life, during the few meaningless days they pass through like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they are gone?
